page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-192 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processors. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server features 192 vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 360 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 1.88 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across both single-core and multi-core operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU benchmark registers at 328676.05, while the single-core score reaches 3451.38. Memory performance is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 18520.89 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 225.4 GB/sec. The system supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions, which accelerate cryptographic and mathematical operations.

Given its high compute density and top-tier performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, this server is suited for high-throughput web serving, large-scale data decompression, and CPU-based machine learning inference. It processed 7B parameter LLM prompts at 450.06 tokens per second. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.88 GB per core and the complete lack of local NVMe storage represent key tradeoffs, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-192 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processors. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores, 360 GB of RAM, and no local storage or GPU accelerators. This hardware configuration delivers top-tier CPU and memory performance, as evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 328676.05 and a PassMark CPU score of 152624.84. Advanced instruction support includes AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. With a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 GB per core and no local disk, this instance is highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy, stateless workloads. It is optimized for high-throughput web serving, Redis databases, multi-threaded decompression, and CPU-based LLM inference, though it is constrained for memory-bound applications.
